lifecycle.ready_for_validation_summary: MT-122 implemented. TWO defects, both fixed. (a) STATIC CHROME: three action rows used a plain ui.horizontal with HARDCODED desired_width values (220.0 and 120.0). At a narrow pane those rows overflowed, and egui's Region::expand_to_include_rect widens a Ui's max_rect over the overflow, so the static row handed EVERY later row a layout width larger than the visible pane. Fixed with horizontal_wrapped plus a fit_width(ui, preferred) helper that clamps to ui.available_width(). (b) RESULT ROW: hit.title is unbounded backend content laid out FIRST left-to-right, so a long title consumed the row and pushed the [source_kind] badge past the pane's right edge, where the results ScrollArea clips it - the operator loses the only at-a-glance signal distinguishing a document hit from a file or loom_block hit. Fixed with MT-119's existing idiom rather than a second pattern: reserve the bounded badge first against the row's right edge via Layout::right_to_left, then let the title truncate into what remains, keeping the full title recoverable through egui's show_tooltip_when_elided. PT-122-2 RED (result-row fix reverted, verbatim): 'MT-122: the [source_kind] badge must render FULLY INSIDE the Find-in-Files pane. rect x=[1132.125, 1183.906] y=[198.000, 208.000] vs pane x=[0.000, 420.000] y=[0.000, 800.000]' - the badge rendered 712px outside a 420px pane. PT-122-2 GREEN (fix applied, verbatim): 'test find_in_files::tests::mt122_result_row_badge_stays_inside_the_find_pane ... ok'. PT-122-3 REGRESSION: the full find_in_files suite is 48 passed / 0 failed, and critically mt119_saved_search_controls_stay_inside_the_find_pane is still green, proving the static-chrome change did not regress MT-119's guard. The RED capture reverted ONLY the result-row fix and restored it through a shell trap, so a failed run could not strand a reverted fix on disk. The guard carries five interlocks that refuse to pass vacuously: I0 fails loudly if the STATIC row regresses (so a future reader is not sent to the wrong file), I1 proves the pane is genuinely bounded using clip_rect rather than the Frame response rect which grows to include overflow, I2 proves the fixture title genuinely overflows at 1.5x the pane width, I4 proves truncation is actually in force, and I5 proves the row's content-derived click route is byte-identical so the layout fix did not change the interaction contract. Implementer evidence only, not validation.

The saved-search Restore/Remove controls consequently land at x=[380.16,433.28] and x=[441.28,496.41] - outside a 420px pane EVEN WITH THE MT-119 FIX APPLIED.

C1-FDELETE-CANVAS.finding: Probe 2 (all sub-conditions of fn::mt109_has_workspace_access): the admin view shows the owner's workspace grant fully valid (active, actions incl. delete, capability fs.write, chain == session chain, policy_version 1 == resource 1 == session 1, creator enabled, owner/space match); the plain record-user signin sees NO grants. Cause of the empty view: protected_resources.external_resource_id is FOR select NONE (schema.surql, protected_resources fields), so a plain record-user signin can never satisfy `resource_id.external_resource_id = $external` — yet the FEMS-only workspace delete passes the same guard in production code. Therefore the product's with_record_user_scope execution context differs from a plain signin and BOTH probes (runs 46, 56) evaluated the guard in the wrong context; clause-1 is not proven to be the failing clause in the real delete.
